scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC5 in Campus 1 reports its default gateway (172.16.10.254)
became unreachable, even though PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same switch
work fine. PC5 still gets link, ARP for its own subnet times
out for everyone except itself. What's wrong with PC5's switch
port?

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch1 eth2 port VLAN membership
Mechanism: switch1's eth2 is the access port for PC5. It was
  moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1 (the unused default
  VLAN). PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10
  semantics, but switch1 now bridges them into VLAN 1 — a
  L2 broadcast domain with no router attached. ARP for the
  gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (eth3-5)
  are unaffected.
Localization: switch1 (eth2 port VLAN assignment)
Root cause: access port eth2 moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 1 on switch1
Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1

line.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

agent.diagnosis_text:
Switch1's access port eth2 — the port serving PC5 — has been
incorrectly assigned to the native VLAN bridge (br_vlan1) instead
of the VLAN 10 bridge (br_vlan10). The switch startup script
(`switch1.startup`) explicitly configures all four PC-facing access
ports (eth2 through eth5) to join br_vlan10 via a `for port in 2 3
4 5` loop. In the live device state, eth3, eth4, and eth5
(serving PC6, PC7, and PC8 respectively) are correctly mastered to
br_vlan10, but eth2 (PC5) is mastered to br_vlan1 — the native VLAN
segment used only for trunk uplink plumbing. Frames originating from
PC5 therefore land in a completely separate Linux bridge domain and
are never forwarded to br_vlan10 members (the other PC ports or the
VLAN 10 trunk sub-interfaces eth0.10 / eth1.10 toward mswitch0).
This is why PC5 can see link (physical layer intact) but ARP
requests to peer VLAN 10 hosts go 100% unanswered (confirmed: arping
from PC5 to PC6 at 172.16.10.6 returned 0/3 replies), and why the
symptom is exclusive to PC5 while PC6/7/8 remain healthy. The root
cause is that switch1.eth2 was reassigned to br_vlan1 post-startup,
placing PC5 on the wrong Layer 2 domain. The corrective fix is to
move the port back: on switch1, run `ip link set eth2 nomaster` then
`ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10`. This restores PC5 to VLAN 10
and immediately restores ARP reachability to the gateway and peer
hosts.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly identifies switch1 as the affected device and repeatedly references it as the location of the misconfigured eth2 port.
The report explicitly identifies switch1's eth2 port and states it is incorrectly mastered to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10 (wrong VLAN membership).
The writeup clearly identifies a port-specific fault (switch1 eth2 moved to br_vlan1) affecting only PC5 and not the host itself, distinguishing it from a host-side problem.
Proposes the required remediation (ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10); the additional nomaster step is harmless and ensures a clean reassignment.

The agent's logs show eth2 is mastered to br_vlan1 while startup config expects eth2..eth5 on br_vlan10; FDB and bridge link outputs plus PC5 arping results support the VLAN-misassignment diagnosis and the proposed fix. Minor truncation/inconsistency in the gateway ARP evidence prevents a perfect score, but the core claims are well-grounded and the causal chain is sound and complete.
